title: The loop: send, receive a tool call, execute, repeat

concept.heading: The agent is a while loop that owns the conversation
paragraphs: Send the messages and the tool list. The model answers with either text or one or more tool calls. If tool calls: validate the arguments, run each tool, append an assistant message carrying the calls and a tool message carrying each result, and send everything again. If text: stop. That loop is the whole agent; frameworks add convenience around it, never a different idea.

The provider wrapper (tools/provider.py, shipped complete) hides every vendor's wire format behind one complete(messages, tools) call that returns a ModelReply. Your loop never sees Gemini's functionCall parts or Groq's OpenAI-style tool_calls, so free tiers can come and go and the loop does not move. The replay provider returns recorded replies, which is how the check stays deterministic and free.

Two safety rails belong in the loop, not in a prompt: max_turns stops a model that never says done, and nothing a tool does may escape as an exception. The next lesson makes every failure a structured error; this lesson makes sure the loop terminates and keeps the transcript honest.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: A Copilot Studio generative orchestrator or an n8n AI Agent node: you configured the tools and watched the run log of calls. Here you write the thing that produces that run log.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: a while loop with a turn budget, json.dumps, list of dicts
pythonBlock.intro: The messages list is the state. Each turn appends; nothing is ever rewritten.
pythonBlock.code:
import json

messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}, {"role": "user", "content": user_message}]
executed = []
for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):
    reply = provider.complete(messages, registry.specs())
    if not reply.wants_tools:
        return LoopResult(final_text=reply.text, stop_reason="final", turns=turn, messages=messages, tool_calls=executed)
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply.text,
                     "tool_calls": [tc.model_dump() for tc in reply.tool_calls]})
    for tc in reply.tool_calls:
        result = registry.call(tc.name, tc.arguments)        # never raises (m1-3)
        messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc.id, "name": tc.name, "content": json.dumps(result)})
        executed.append(ExecutedCall(id=tc.id, name=tc.name, arguments=tc.arguments, result=result))
# out of turns -> stop_reason="max_turns", final_text=None

spec: Implement run_loop per the docstring: system + user on turn 1, registry.specs() as the tool list, tool results appended as tool messages with content=json.dumps(result).
Stop on a reply without tool calls (stop_reason final) or after max_turns (stop_reason max_turns, final_text None). Record every executed call in result.tool_calls.
Until m1-3 exists, call registry.call and let its NotImplementedError surface; the check's scripted cases are written to pass once both lessons are done. Build m1-2 and m1-3 together if you prefer.

Get one free-tier key (Gemini or Groq, no card), put LLM_PROVIDER and the key in middleware/.env, and run the live smoke test: uv run --directory middleware pytest checks/m1/test_m1_2_tool_loop.py -m live -q. It is skipped when no key is set.
Read provider.py once end to end. It is plumbing you will own for clients.
